title: lipid-2d: bonded 3-bead amphiphiles (Cooke-Kremer-Deserno, implicit solvent) self-assemble from a random gas into material bilayer ribbons, but not (yet) into closed 2D vesicles
summary: New class: 800 three-bead lipids (head + two tails, FENE bonds, a straightening spring, WCA cores, a broad cos^2 tail-tail attraction as the only hydrophobic force) under overdamped Langevin dynamics in an 80x80 periodic box. From a uniform random gas they form bilayer ribbons with heads on both faces and tails inside within t~500 (ribbons.png; kT=0.55-0.6, larger heads b_HH=1.3), which lengthen, bend and fuse over t~3600; at kT=1 they stay a gas, at kT<=0.5 or equal head/tail size they freeze into disordered clusters, and at 1.75x density they jam into short wiggly bilayers. No ribbon closed into a ring enclosing solvent at the 4 points tried (in 2D the open edge costs only two end caps, so closure needs long ribbons). With the optional membrane chemistry (precursor lipids with hydrophilic tails convert where they touch existing bilayer tails), active lipids rise from 30% to 83% by t=1800 and the new lipid is added to existing ribbons.
